$note: Written after looking at every shot at 0%, 33%, 66% and 94% in out/.frames-<id>/, plus the rendered reel. Scores are one person's judgement out of ten and are deliberately NOT computed: every reel this repo has shipped broken passed the computed gates.
question: Why Does This Tiny Strait Matter to the World?
verdict: It shows the strait now. Two coasts, the water between them, one lane in and one lane out, and a dimension across the gap reading 21 MILES -- built from a sentence that says 'twenty-one miles across' and 'northern shore, southern shore', with no map of Hormuz anywhere in the repository. Eleven of twenty-two shots carry it. The chokepoint line gets a hatched closure and a hazard marker on the lane, which is the argument the whole episode is making, drawn.
whatWorked: The map fired on six of nine lines and each one is the right graphic for its sentence: a width where the line states a width, two lanes where it says one in and one out, a closure where it says one tanker shuts it.
The 21 MILES dimension is correct. It was 20 until the hyphenated-compound bug was found -- a drawn figure contradicting its own narration is worse than no figure.
cold-noir over the wash field remains the strongest ground of the five: the schematic reads as a chart rather than as an illustration.
The measurement bar carries 20,000,000 BARRELS, a unit the matcher did not know before.
Nothing claims survey precision: the coasts are generated from the line's seed and the plate says SCHEMATIC -- NOT TO SCALE on every frame.

whatFailed.what: Nine of twenty-two shots are still typography.
whatFailed.why: Five are title slates, which is deliberate. The other four are genuinely abstract lines -- 'a fifth of everything the world burns', 'every fuel price on earth moves' -- and words are the honest representation for those.

whatFailed.what: The chain from one grounded tanker to a global price is still asserted, not drawn.
whatFailed.why: A map can show a blockage. It has no way to show a consequence propagating out of the frame; that needs a dependency or flow-out-of-system primitive that does not exist.

whatFailed.what: The single-landmass variant reads as an abstract hexagon rather than as land.
whatFailed.why: With no two-shore signal the builder makes one blob from six control points. It is honest but it is not evocative.
